nodes.summary: Let $(r_i)$, $(s_i)$ and $N$ be Euclidean switching data with $r_0$ odd and $r_1$ even. Then $2|s_1| = r_0 - 1$ and $2|s_2| = r_1$ hold simultaneously if and only if $r_1 = 2$.
nodes.title: Both first inverses extremal, odd–even case

nodes.summary: Let $(r_i)$, $(s_i)$ and $N$ be Euclidean switching data with $r_0$ and $r_1$ both odd. Then $2|s_1| = r_0 - 1$ and $2|s_2| = r_1 - 1$ hold simultaneously if and only if $r_0 = r_1 + 2$.
nodes.title: Both first inverses extremal, odd–odd case

nodes.summary: Let $(r_i)$, $(s_i)$ and $N$ be Euclidean switching data with $r_0$ even and $r_1$ odd. Then $2|s_1| < r_0$ or $2|s_2| < r_1 - 1$; that is, $|s_1| < r_0/2$ or $|s_2| < (r_1 - 1)/2$.
nodes.title: First inverses not both extremal, even–odd case

nodes.summary: Let $m$ and $n$ be coprime positive integers, and let $x$ and $y$ be integers with $xm + yn = 1$. Then $xm \equiv 1 \pmod{n}$ and $yn \equiv 1 \pmod{m}$; that is, $x$ is an inverse of $m$ modulo $n$ and $y$ is an inverse of $n$ modulo $m$.
nodes.title: Bézout coefficients are modular inverses

nodes.summary: Let $m > n > 1$ be integers, write $g = \gcd(m, n)$, and let $(r_i)$, $(s_i)$ and $N$ be Euclidean switching data with $r_0 = m/g$ and $r_1 = n/g$. Then for all integers $x$ and $y$ with $xm + yn = g$, we have $|s_2| \le |x|$ and $|s_1| \le |y|$.
nodes.title: The Euclidean Bézout coefficients are smallest in absolute value

nodes.summary: Let $m > n > 1$ be integers, write $g = \gcd(m, n)$, and let $(r_i)$, $(s_i)$ and $N$ be Euclidean switching data with $r_0 = m/g$ and $r_1 = n/g$. Then $s_2 m + s_1 n = g$, $s_2$ is the least absolute inverse of $m/g$ modulo $n/g$, and $s_1$ is the least absolute inverse of $n/g$ modulo $m/g$.
nodes.title: The Euclidean Bézout coefficients are least absolute inverses

nodes.summary: Let $m > n > 1$ be integers, write $g = \gcd(m, n)$, and let $(r_i)$, $(s_i)$ and $N$ be Euclidean switching data with $r_0 = m/g$ and $r_1 = n/g$. Then for all integers $x$ and $y$ with $xm + yn = g$, we have $s_2^2 + s_1^2 \le x^2 + y^2$.
nodes.title: Rankin's minimality of the Euclidean Bézout pair

nodes.summary: Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers with $\gcd(m, n) = 1$, and let $t$ be an integer with $\gcd(|t|, n) = 1$. Then $m = kn + t$ for some integer $k$ if and only if there are integers $x$ and $y$ with $xt \equiv 1 \pmod{n}$, $yn \equiv 1 \pmod{m}$ and $xm + yn = 1$.
nodes.title: Modular inverse switching

nodes.summary: A natural number $N$, a sequence $r_0, r_1, \dots$ of natural numbers and a sequence $s_0, s_1, \dots$ of integers form Euclidean switching data when $N \ge 1$; $r_0 > r_1 > \cdots > r_{N+1} = 1$, with $r_0, \dots, r_{N+1}$ all positive; for each $i = 1, \dots, N$ there is a positive integer $q_i$ with $r_{i-1} = q_i r_i + r_{i+1}$; $s_{N+1} = 1$; and $s_{i+1} r_{i-1} + s_i r_i = 1$ for each $i = 1, \dots, N$.
nodes.title: Euclidean switching data

nodes.summary: Let $(r_i)$, $(s_i)$ and $N$ be Euclidean switching data. Then for every $i$ with $1 \le i \le N + 1$, $s_i$ is the least absolute inverse of $r_i$ modulo $r_{i-1}$.
nodes.title: Every switching inverse is a least absolute inverse

nodes.summary: Let $r_0, r_1, \ldots$ be natural numbers, $s_0, s_1, \ldots$ integers and $N \ge 1$ such that $(r, s, N)$ is Euclidean switching data: $r_0 > r_1 > \cdots > r_{N+1} = 1$ are the successive remainders of the Euclidean algorithm, $s_{N+1} = 1$, and $s_{i+1} r_{i-1} + s_i r_i = 1$ for $1 \le i \le N$. nodes.title: Least absolute inverses propagate down the Euclidean sequence

nodes.summary: For integers $x$ and $a$ and a natural number $n$, $x$ is the least absolute inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ when $xa \equiv 1 \pmod{n}$ and $-n < 2x \le n$, that is, when $x$ is an inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ in the half-open interval $-n/2 < x \le n/2$.
nodes.title: Least absolute inverse
